## Intent
Hypothesis: scalar AoS codegen with identity ordering and register-resident death verdict can approach competitive performance without vectorization or intermediate storage.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/particle AoS struct offers 32 hot bytes to loop 1 (age+pos+seed+vel, 47%) and 28 to loop 2 (color+pos, 41%) — over half each line fill is dead weight. No intermediate storage keeps the verdict in registers, but identity ordering prevents hot-field compaction. The approach is purely scalar: branchy respawn in loop 1, select-based blending in loop 2. L1d spills at N≈963, L2 at N≈61680; the sub-50% hot fraction roughly halves effective hot-set thresholds.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/particle is flat: 7.27 at N=380 (L1d) to 7.97 at N=10000 (L2), settling to ~7.2–7.4 in DRAM. No spill knee — the 47% hot fraction means transitions move mostly dead bytes, and the 98-insn/iter loop-1 compute amortizes bandwidth. L1d→L2 at N≈963 is invisible (7.48→7.55); L2→DRAM at N≈61680 shows slight improvement (7.45→7.30), as stride-68B prefetching is as effective from DRAM as L2. The dense grid resolves no knee because the algo is compute/branch-bound.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 9.47 GB/s (q=0.01, N=150000) — 32% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling, 3.2x above the 2.274 ns/p floor. Never bandwidth-bound: DRAM sustains ~9.2 GB/s. At q=0.01 it is compute-bound (65–72% compute, 4–7% branch_flush). As q rises, branch_flush dominates: 21% at q=0.1, 32% at q=0.25, 36% at q=0.5; achieved BW drops 9.35→5.32 GB/s (q=0.01→0.5, N=380). It is 1.0x baseline everywhere (it IS the baseline) and 1.6–2.5x slower than the winner, widening from 1.6x at q=0.01/N=10000 to 2.5x at q=0.5/N=100000.

## Assembly
Entirely scalar: 1 vector instruction (movi.2d) out of 302; all FP on s-registers (fmul s, fadd s, fcmp s). Loop 1 (L40-L59): 98 insns/iter, 11 cond branches, stride-68B scalar loads (ldr s, ldp s); branchy respawn (b.ge, b.gt) blocks vectorization. Loop 2 (L63-L64): 147 insns/iter, 15 cond branches, 18 csel for blending, 16 byte-granular scatter stores (strb w,[x1] at 0x10004db70) with ldrb loads — each channel loaded, clamped (cmp #0xff, csel), stored individually. The scalar FP chain over 32 hot bytes makes compute dominate; strb scatter caps streaming.

## Verdict
Refuted — 1.0x baseline but 1.6–2.5x slower than the winner at every point, never exceeding 32% of ceiling (9.47 vs 29.9 GB/s) and 3.2x above the memory floor. Branch_flush rises 4.3%→36% as q goes 0.01→0.5, the 47%/41% hot-byte fractions waste over half the bandwidth, and the scalar codegen (1/302 vector insns, 16 strb/iter) cannot vectorize or stream — it is compute-and-branch-bound, not memory-bound.
